## Background

<!-- Optional. Inline math goes between single dollar signs; a display equation
between double dollar signs. LaTeX syntax:
https://www.overleaf.com/learn/latex/Mathematical_expressions -->

With selection intensity $i$ and heritability $h^2$, the breeder's equation
gives the expected per-generation response

$$
R = i \, h^2 \, \sigma_P .
$$

## Analysis

<!-- One runnable chunk per idea. `#| label:` names the chunk, `#| fig-cap:`
captions the figure. Add `#| echo: false` to hide code entirely, or
`#| eval: false` to show code without running it. Always set a seed. -->

```{julia}
#| label: fig-genetic-gain
#| fig-cap: "Simulated mean breeding value over generations of truncation selection"
#| warning: false

using Random, Statistics, Plots
Random.seed!(42)

n_individuals, n_generations = 200, 15
selection_fraction, heritability = 0.2, 0.4

population = randn(n_individuals)
mean_bv = [mean(population)]

for _ in 1:n_generations
    n_selected = round(Int, n_individuals * selection_fraction)
    parent_mean = mean(sort(population, rev = true)[1:n_selected])
    # Offspring regress toward the selected parents' mean, scaled by
    # heritability, plus fresh noise each generation.
    global population = parent_mean * heritability .+ randn(n_individuals) .* (1 - heritability)
    push!(mean_bv, mean(population))
end

plot(0:n_generations, mean_bv,
    xlabel = "Generation", ylabel = "Mean breeding value",
    legend = false, linewidth = 2, marker = :circle)
```
